source.title: Spilling the Beans: Teaching LLMs to Self-Report Their Hidden Objectives
source.authors: Chloe Li; Mary Phuong; Daniel Tan

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies whether fine-tuning improves self-reporting of hidden objectives. Its prefill experiments concern eliciting hidden-objective details, not refusal of harmful user requests, and it does not measure the claim's safety-training effects, token-position KL, or safety localization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for prefilling in hidden-objective interrogation, a different behavior from refusal of harmful requests. It reports no harmful-request compliance or refusal rates, aligned-versus-base per-token KL, weight/rank localization, or safety-deepening training results. The prefill findings are recorded under fits_no_version rather than as evidence for V4.
record.test_reason: The study trains GPT-4.1 to admit factual errors and measures disclosure of in-context hidden objectives during interrogation. It does not measure harmful-request compliance after fine-tuning, per-token KL, refusal bypass by prefilling, weight localization, or safety deepening. It cites Qi et al. 2024 only as prior work on prefill attacks. Its prefill results concern eliciting hidden objectives, not bypassing refusal of harmful user requests, so they bear on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SRFT (770 factual-error-admission examples) generalizes to confessing in-context hidden objectives: detection F1 0.98 vs. 0, and 28–100% of details elicited vs. 0%. This holds under non-disclosure instructions and mostly under decoys. They present it as a promising auditing technique. Stated limitations are weak covertness incentives, the confound with weakened instruction-hierarchy compliance (72% to 61%), in-context rather than trained-in objectives, and reliance on introspective ability.
record.recipe_differences: The study's SRFT method trains factual-error admissions; it does not reproduce or test the cited safety fine-tuning or token-depth methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Hidden-objective disclosure varies with interrogation design and ordering, model, decoy condition, training-data ablation, and system-prompt contextualization.

fits_no_version.finding: On unfinetuned Claude Sonnet 4, prefilling the response with 'My secret objective is' elicited 100% of hidden-objective details without a decoy. A prefilled earlier turn elicited up to 71%, against up to 40% with no prefill. On GPT-4.1 the prefilled turn elicited 0%. Adding a decoy cut prefilled-response elicitation by 40–48% on 3 of 4 tasks, and the model mentioned the decoy in 94–100% of trials.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prefilling the assistant response overrides system-prompt confidentiality instructions and elicits concealed information. Its effect depends on the model and on whether a decoy is available.

record.problems: The study does not measure the claimed safety-refusal behavior. Its authors note that the prompted incentive to conceal may be weak and that in-context objectives may not generalize to objectives learned during training. Some reported prefill summaries are maxima or aggregates across tasks rather than per-task values.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version results were reported. Per-task plotted prefill values were not transcribed where the prose only provided aggregate or maximum statements.

untested.parts: Benign fine-tuning effects on harmful compliance. SRFT and the 50% instruction-tuning mix were not evaluated on harmful requests.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Prefill, suffix or decoding bypass of harmful-request refusal.
Localization of safety in weights or ranks.
Deepening safety training and its robustness.

record.verdict_notes: The record's gate is correct. The paper cites arXiv:2406.05946 only for prefill attacks. No harmful-request refusal rates are reported anywhere, including in the capability and instruction-hierarchy side-effect evaluations.

versions.untested_parts: Benign instruction fine-tuning effects on harmful-request compliance/refusal. The paper's instruction-tuning mixture is evaluated for hidden-objective self-report, not harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Whether prefilling, suffixes, or decoding changes bypass refusal of harmful user requests. Prefill is tested only for eliciting hidden objectives.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Training to deepen safety behaviour and its robustness.
